metadata.name: dsh-neverdie

paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) host plugin — auto-revives sessions whose turn was killed by a process exit (
'Task stopped') after restart, and re-arms their active goals
# Neverdie
**Automatically revives DeepSeek Harness (DSH) sessions whose turn was killed by a process exit.** W
hen the host dies mid-turn, every session that was working ends up frozen behind a *"Task stopped —
The DSH process exited before this turn finished…"* banner, dead until a human types something. Neve
rdie removes the human from that loop: after DSH restarts, the killed sessions come back to life on
their own and keep working — and their active goals get re-armed so autonomous goal rounds continue.
## Why
A DSH process that is killed, crashes, or times out during shutdown takes every running session down
with it, and the cut-short turn shows up two different ways depending on how the process went:
- **Hard crash** (SIGKILL, OOM) — the log ends inside an open turn; restart recovery synthesizes a `

turn/end` closer with reason `interrupted`.
- **Graceful exit / restart** — the dying process gets t
o close the running turn itself, as reason `aborted` with cause `disposed`; the aborted tool call le
aves an *"Error: tool call aborted"* message as the visible tail of the conversation.
Either way the session sits idle, dead until a human types something — even though the durable sessi
on log, the workspace, and the model context are all intact. All the work was *interrupted*, not los
t. Long-running jobs (overnight builds, multi-hour agent tasks, goal-driven rounds) deserved better
than "click Send again in the morning".
Neverdie is a host-side Cordis plugin that scans once after every boot, finds exactly the sessions t
hat were mid-turn when the previous process died, and re-prompts them with a short configurable mess
age so the agent resumes where it stopped.
## Features
- **Precise corpse detection** — a session is revived only when the tail of its balanced log is a `t
urn/end` closed `interrupted` (hard crash) or `aborted` with cause `disposed` (graceful exit / resta
rt). Deliberate stops (`aborted` cause `user`/`parent`/`hook`), sessions that ended normally, and se
ssions that already have newer input are never touched — matching on the abort *cause* rather than t

he visible "Error: tool call aborted" text is what keeps user-stopped sessions dead
- **Survives res
tart bookkeeping** — the tail walker skips generation markers (e.g. `session/end-seed`) that DSH app
ends after a restart, and synthesizes the interrupted closers in memory for cold logs, so detection

works whether or not the session was reopened first
- **Live-but-idle counts as dead** — the reconne
cting web client resumes a session's log without resuming its work; neverdie treats that idle state

as a corpse too
- **Goal re-arm** — goal activation is process-local, so the restart that killed the
turn also disarmed the session's goal. Neverdie re-arms *active* goals through the supported `goals
.resume` path, so automatic continuation rounds keep running. Paused, blocked, complete, or round-ex

hausted goals are respected as-is
- **Crash-loop guard** — at most `maxRevives` consecutive neverdie
revives per session since the last genuine user message; a host that keeps dying cannot burn tokens

forever, and one real user message resets the budget
- **Auditable** — every revive is a normal use
r message tagged with the merge-extensible source kind `neverdie`, visible in the transcript and cou
ntable from the session log, plus a `[neverdie]` line in the host journal
## How it works
1. The host process dies mid-turn. The plugin dies with it — nothing can act at the moment of death.
2. Whatever supervises DSH (e.g. systemd `Restart=on-failure`) starts a new process; the plugin arm

s and waits `delaySeconds` for boot to settle.
3. One scan: list sessions cheaply, then fully read t

he balanced log of each fresh, non-archived, root candidate.
4. A backward walker finds the log's la
st turn end; only an `interrupted` one or an `aborted`-with-`disposed`-cause one, with no newer turn

, message, or pending inbox input, qualifies.
5. For each corpse: `resolveAgent` (resumes the cold s

ession), re-arm its active goal if disarmed, queue the revive message, flush to durable storage.
6.
The agent continues the interrupted task. If the host dies again, the next boot repeats the cycle wi
thin the revive budget.
## Configuration
| Option | Type | Default | Description |

| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Master switch |
| `delaySeconds` | `number` | `10` | Wait after h

ost start before the startup scan (0–600) |
| `maxAgeMinutes` | `number` | `60` | Only revive sessio

ns whose interrupted turn is younger than this (1–1440) |
| `maxRevives` | `number` | `5` | Max cons

ecutive neverdie revives per session without genuine user input (0–10) |
| `reviveMessage` | `string

` | *(see below)* | The message injected to revive a session |
| `resumeGoals` | `boolean` | `true`
| Re-arm active-but-disarmed goals during revival |
Default revive message:
> `[neverdie] The DSH process exited before the previous turn could finish, so that turn was closed.
Continue the interrupted task from where it stopped. Tool calls that were cut off have unknown outc
omes — inspect their effects before retrying them.`
## Notes & limitations
- **Restart must come from outside.** Neverdie revives sessions *after* the host is back; it cannot

restart the host itself. Pair it with a supervisor such as systemd (`Restart=on-failure`).
- **A lit
eral empty prompt is not possible.** The harness rejects whitespace-only prompt content, so revival

sends a real (short, configurable) message instead.
- **Root conversations only.** Subagent children

are left to their parent sessions, which the parent's own revival reconciles.
- **Freshness bounded
.** Corpses older than `maxAgeMinutes` stay dead — raise the window if your host can be down for a l
es older than `maxAgeMinutes` stay dead — raise the window if your host can be down for a long time.
